entry.title: OpenAI's $70B Run Rate Meets AI's Infrastructure Challenge
entry.summary: loomberg’s Ed Ludlow breaks down OpenAI's latest annualized revenue, expected to reach or exceed $70 billion by the end of the year. Plus, Oracle keeps several data centers on track by relying on truck deliveries of natural gas, and a conversation with Kleiner Perkins partner Ilya Fushman on the mega AI IPO pipeline and the future of physical AI. (Source: Bloomberg)

entry.title: From Anthropic to Waymo: Kleiner Perkins Bets on AI’s Next Act
entry.summary: Kleiner Perkins partner Ilya Fushman says AI is still in the early stages of reshaping the economy, with opportunities extending from frontier models like Anthropic to consumer agents, autonomous vehicles and robotics. entry.title: AI Buildout is Boom 'Not Bubble,' Says Jared Gross
entry.summary: Credit markets are again becoming jittery over the prospects of more mega debt deals hitting a market already flush with financings to pay for the AI arms race. Jared Gross, Head of Institutional Portfolio Strategy at JPMorgan Asset Management, discusses AI asset allocation and why he believes the AI buildout is indeed a boom, not a bubble. (Source: Bloomberg)

entry.title: We Want to 'Dominate' US: Revolut's Storonsky
entry.summary: Revolut CEO Nik Storonsky lays out the fintech’s ambitions to crack the US market and take on established players including JPMorgan and American Express. He says Revolut plans to build out a full digital banking offer, from credit cards to loans, while using AI and automation to reshape how customers bank. How the company trades will be the next test in London’s efforts to revitalize its capital markets. entry.title: Nvidia-Backed Firmus IPO Collapses as AI Valuation Concerns Grow
entry.summary: Firmus abandoned its attempt at one of Australia’s biggest-ever initial public offerings, after the Nvidia-backed data center company failed to lure global investors who’ve grown increasingly skittish over frothy AI valuations. (Source: Bloomberg)

entry.summary: AI is driving one of the largest capital spending cycles in decades, creating new questions around how that investment will be financed and where the risks and opportunities will emerge across credit markets. entry.title: Nvidia-Backed Firmus Is Set to Postpone IPO, Weigh Private Round
entry.summary: Australian data center company Firmus Grid Ltd. is set to postpone its initial public offering, and the company is weighing a private funding round instead, according to people familiar with the matter.

entry.title: OpenAI Investment Boosts Tiger Global's Hedge Fund
entry.summary: OpenAI is in talks to raise $30 billion at a $1.4 trillion valuation, with Tiger Global poised for a paper profit of $5 billion. Hema Parmar reports on "Bloomberg Open Interest." (Source: Bloomberg)

entry.summary: Boyu Capital and IDG Capital led the funding round, and existing shareholders Tencent, HSG (formerly known as Sequoia China), ZhenFund, and others also participated.

entry.title: JPMorgan Private Bank Says AI Set to Drive Strong Earnings
entry.summary: Nataliia Lipikhina, head of EMEA equity strategy at JPMorgan Private Bank, discusses how artificial intelligence continues to underpin global equity markets, particularly the tech sector. "I think the market comes to realization that actually the AI story continues," she tells Bloomberg Television. "Demand is still really strong, and supply is still constrained," Lipikhina adds. entry.title: Isomorphic Labs Seeks Funding at Valuation of $40 Billion
entry.summary: Isomorphic Labs, an AI-powered drug discovery startup spun out of Alphabet Inc.’s Google DeepMind, is in early talks to raise new funds at a valuation of at least $40 billion, according to people familiar with the effort. Bloomberg's Neil Campling has the details. (Source: Bloomberg)

entry.title: Why Investors Are Skeptical Over Australian Data Center Company Firmus's IPO
entry.summary: Nvidia-backed data center company Firmus's IPO, set to be among the biggest listings in Australia, has become "unusually polarizing," Australian portfolio manager Jun Bei Liu of Ten Cap says. (Source: Bloomberg)

entry.title: Goldman Says Middle Managers at Risk as New Hires Oversee AI
entry.summary: The newest hires in finance won’t have to wait years to become managers. They’ll be overseeing artificial intelligence agents from the time they join, raising the question of what happens to the current middle managers, according to Goldman Sachs Group Inc.’s Kevin Sneader.
